ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Vincent van Gogh

code.originalText: Three-month review with the 12-week metabolic check

text.paragraph: Three-month review with the 12-week metabolic check. [S]

Mr. van Gogh returns three months after his first visit, fifteen weeks after aripiprazole was started in hospital, fasting for his blood tests. He has had no voices, suspiciousness, or confusion since the six-week visit. He takes aripiprazole 10 mg and naltrexone every morning. He sleeps about seven hours and goes to bed by midnight; he noticed once that after a late night of work he felt a rush of ideas the next day, and he went to bed early as his plan says. He paints most days, outdoors now that spring has come, and has sold two paintings. He drinks one glass of wine with dinner on most days and none on two days a week. His appetite is a little greater than before. His mood is steady; he has not had thoughts of suicide or self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-20; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 65.7 kg, BMI 22.7; waist 87 cm; blood pressure 122/78, pulse 74
No akathisia, rigidity, tremor, or abnormal movements
Euthymic; organized; no psychotic features; speech normal in rate

First episode of psychosis with mood features: weeks of very little sleep, intense work and expansive plans, then acute confusion, hallucinations and suspiciousness with self-injury, and low mood since discharge. Diagnosis provisional; differential: bipolar I disorder with psychotic features, brief psychotic or schizophreniform disorder, alcohol withdrawal delirium or alcohol-induced psychotic disorder, and psychosis related to focal epilepsy. Synthetic modern episode linked to his documented first crisis
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented first crisis. Unspecified psychosis is coded because the cause is not yet established; the retrospective diagnoses stay in the claims.
Alcohol use disorder, moderate (heavy daily wine and anise spirits before the episode); synthetic modern episode linked to his documented heavy drinking
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented drinking and its retrospective interpretation.
Self-injury to the left ear during the acute confusional episode, without suicidal intent; wound healed after surgical care in hospital
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented injury; no detail of the injury is recorded.
Akathisia from aripiprazole, two weeks after the dose was increased to 15 mg; treated by returning to 10 mg and short-term propranolol; resolved
S — Synthetic medication side effect; not a historical claim.

list.item:
First episode of psychosis with mood features, provisional diagnosis, in remission (F29). Remission for about two months. The day of racing ideas after a late night was an early warning sign that he managed well; it did not progress. The 12-week metabolic check is normal: fasting glucose 94 mg/dL, A1c 5.4%, total cholesterol 191, LDL 112, HDL 50 and triglycerides 142 mg/dL; weight up 2.7%, below the 5% that would call for action. Antipsychotic treatment continues after a first episode; the length of treatment will be decided with him later in the year. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm; the safety plan is current. [S]
Continue aripiprazole 10 mg daily.
Keep to the sleep plan and call the team after two short nights or more racing ideas.
Yearly glucose, A1c and lipids from now.

Alcohol use disorder on naltrexone (F10.20). PEth down to 46 ng/mL; AST 33, ALT 31 and GGT 49 U/L, now normal. [S]
Continue naltrexone and thiamine.
Liver tests and PEth at six months.
